sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: the vision, knowledge and road examinations
Audience: every first-time Tennessee Class D applicant about to sit the knowledge test and book a road test, plus new residents checking which tests they must take.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the chapter describes the knowledge test the product prepares for [A01] and the road test scoring and failure rules that follow it [A03].
Level: procedural recall with a few exact thresholds (vision standard, waiting periods, error bands, equipment counts); low conceptual load.
Prerequisites: the license-class, application and graduated-license chapters, which decide which tests and documents apply.

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.
